answer: An agent economy can require every participant to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its actions count toward reputation or governance. Sybil identities then do not multiply influence for free: each needs its own capital, and proven double-signing or coordinated fraud burns the bond. The haven of cheap throwaway accounts becomes a ledge over real losses; even a saffron-colored avatar still has to put value at risk. This raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the influence they seek, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
